title: Mail and Calendar agents put cards on the glance screen; assistant pane and glance panel polish
body:
Stacked on #263 (`feat/l0-chat-host`), which is stacked on #261. Like #263, this builds only with `.sources` at OctoSense-org/OctoScript#53 (3ca709c) and OctoSense-org/OctoScript-Makepad#68 (51c4c51); GitHub CI on the pinned runtime fails until those merge and the pins move.

## What it does

**App agents publish cards to the glance screen**
- **Mail**: Mail's agent gets `mail.notify`. The mail host service fills a fixed L0 notice card and publishes it as Mail. The model never writes card code.
- **Calendar** (new desktop system app, `os.calendar`): its agent gets `calendar.events`, `add_event`, `remove_event` (destructive, so the person approves it), `notify` (an event card) and `agenda` (the next three events). They run on a new host service, `apps/calendar/host-service`. It takes the `calendar` id, so Makepad's example Calendar leaves the catalog.
- **Executor rule**: App Hub has no `calendar` capability, so a system app's own namespace (`os.calendar` → `calendar`) runs on its own host service without a grant. Every other family still needs one.

**Glance screen**
- A new card opens the glance panel and shows the newest card first. Cards in the panel go through the L0 translation, so tiles keep their colours and chips keep their labels. A tile can be up to 440 pt tall, and the wheel scrolls a card at a time.
- A bell in the bar counts the cards and lights up when new ones arrive. "At a glance" sits in the menu after Apps.
- A click on a toast now reaches the toast, even when a pane or window is under it.

**Assistant pane** (the system chat and "Ask <app>")
- On a desktop it opens as a medium pane at the left. You can move and resize it, and a double-click on the header puts it back. It follows the theme, and the approval sheets now stay above it.
- Replies render Markdown. Wrapping is CJK-aware, using `wrap_styled`, which every surface uses through `ShellDraw::wrap`. The transcript is laid out again only when it changes.
- The prompt takes up to 8 lines, and Shift+Return starts a new line. It has a blinking caret, keyboard and mouse selection, and copy, cut and paste. On a desktop it takes the keyboard when it opens, so the macOS input method composes in it right away.
- Fixes: the pane's `#[redraw]` field was `draw_bg`, which it never draws, so drags and scrolls did not repaint. The pane also no longer runs past the window or sits under the developer-mode banner.

**Fonts**
- The shell's drawing kit used to name JetBrains Mono. It now uses the theme's font roles (regular, bold, code), like the apps. Glance cards that name no font also use those roles instead of the backend's Roboto.

## Checked
- `cargo test -p octosense-shell --features app-hub --lib`: 738 passed.
- `cargo test -p octosense-mail-service -p octosense-calendar-service`: passed.
- `cargo check --locked -p octosense --features mobile-apps`: passed.
- Hidden `--remote` runs on macOS with deepseek-v4-flash:
  - The system agent asked Mail's agent and then Calendar's agent for cards. Calendar went through the first-use sheet, added an event, and its card opened the panel.
  - Drag, resize, caret, selection, Markdown, Chinese wrapping and the theme were all checked.
  - Copy and cut need the platform's menu keys, which a remote run cannot send, so the composer's tests cover them.
- **Unverified:** the phone, where Calendar is not packed.

## Follow-ups
- An App Hub `calendar` capability, so Calendar's own window can list its events.
- Mail's read tools: `mail.accounts` answers an array, and octos needs object output schemas.

title: Craft engines reach agents: Sheets' sheets.* tools, Photos' photos.info, per-engine containment
body:
Closes the agent gap of ADR 0013: the two craft engines are now reachable by agents, not only by `host.request`.

## Sheets (native app)
- `native-apps.json`: Sheets declares its agent (`octos.*`) and nine `sheets.*` tools; `sheets.get` and `sheets.eval` are shareable read tools the system agent may call (`agent.system_tools`). Generated blocks regenerated (`native_apps.rs`, `native_agents.rs`).
- New `crates/shell/src/host_tools/engines.rs`: an executor the relay prefers over the AI bus; it renames `sheets.<tool>` → `sheet.<tool>` and runs it on the sheet service in process, as `"sheets"` (`octosense-sheets-service::may_call` takes the native app now).
- `sheet.eval` without `book` answers a plain calculation, so one read tool works with no session.

## Photos (script app)
- Photos' namespace is its own service now, as Mail's and News's: `octosense-photo-service::register_photos()` answers `photos.info` on the photo engine and `photos.notify` through the shell's notice hook (`on_notify(glance_notice::notify)`); the notice service no longer stands in for Photos.
- `apps/photos/bundle/tools.json` adds `photos.info` (read, host-service, not shareable). Manifest unchanged: no new capability.

## Containment fix (both engines)
Both services rooted I/O at the shared `.host` directory itself, so `sheet.export`/photo saves could write into another service's data (for example `calendar/events.json`). Each engine now works strictly inside its own area, `<host>/sheet` and `<host>/photo`.

## Tests and docs
- Service suites extended (area containment, bookless eval, notify hook, gates); `host_tools`, `glance`, `apps::`, `system_chat` suites green from `phone/` (mobile-apps); pinned-surface tests updated (Photos split from the notify-only trio; stale "sheets declares no tools" fixtures in Rust and Python tests moved to `reference`).
- Live shell (hidden window, remote): `system-call:sheets.eval {"formula":"=1+2*3"}` → `{"value":7.0,"ok":true}` through the real relay and engine; startup log shows the notice service answering only `["os.maps","os.ai-providers","os.youtube"]`. Photos' own-agent live path is exercised through the registry-backed tests only: a cold shell gates a script agent behind first-use consent, so the system-call probe cannot reach it by design.
- `apps/AGENTS.md`, root `AGENTS.md`, `apps/README.md` + `README.zh-CN.md` updated together.

title: Engine agent tools: the system agent reaches the ten ADR 0013 engines
body:
ADR 0013 decision 3 says the first deliverable per engine is the host service and its agent tools. The ten services are already on main. This PR adds their agent tools and lets the system agent (the Assistant) call them.

## Design

- **Tools ship with each service.** Each engine has `apps/<family>/host-service/tools.json` in App Hub's `tools.json` shape, exposed as `pub const TOOLS_JSON`. Every tool is `implemented_by: "host-service"`, runs on the method of its own name (no `host_method`), and has object input and output schemas. The schemas mirror the service's real arguments, caps and answers. Inputs use `additionalProperties: false`. Outputs declare only the fields the service always sets. Each crate's tests load the manifest with App Hub's own loader (`ToolManifest::load(json, family, ToolHost::Contained, false)`, the same path a bundle's `tools.json` takes). They also check octos's object rule and that every tool names a method the service dispatches. So a bad schema fails the crate's own tests.
- **One virtual owner per engine.** No app ships these tools, so `crates/shell/src/host_tools/engines.rs` declares each engine's tools under `os.<family>` and installs an `EngineExecutor` for it. The executor routes through `script_apps::HostServiceExecutor` with `app: "os.<family>"`, `families: {<family>}`, an identity method map, and the host dir `<apps root>/.host` resolved at each call. Registration sits next to the engine service registrations in `apps::register_host_services`, behind `#[cfg(feature = "app-hub")]`. The Sheets path (`EngineExecutor::sheets()`, `sheets.*` → `sheet.*`) behaves as before, and its test is unchanged.
- **System-agent grant.** `ENGINE_TOOLS` in `system_chat/grants.rs` is a reviewed narrow grant like `CALENDAR_TOOLS`.
- **Errors name files relative to the engine's area.** effectcraft put the absolute host path it was handed (the person's home directory) into its error text. The executor removes the host's own spelling of the area from engine error messages. Answers pass through unchanged; the services already make them area-relative.

### The grant (43 tools)

- `word.info`, `word.text`, `word.inspect`, `word.convert`, `word.new`
- `deck.info`, `deck.text`, `deck.render`, `deck.new`, `deck.convert`
- `cad.info`, `cad.entities`, `cad.measure`, `cad.render`, `cad.convert`
- `light.info`, `light.controls`, `light.develop`, `light.batch`
- `sound.info`, `sound.peaks`, `sound.convert`, `sound.trim`, `sound.mix`
- `design.info`, `design.render`, `design.export`
- `film.info`, `film.project.info`, `film.frame`, `film.export`
- `effect.info`, `effect.render`, `effect.export_lottie`, `effect.import_lottie`
- `vector.info`, `vector.convert`, `vector.render`
- `pdf.info`, `pdf.text`, `pdf.render`, `pdf.merge`, `pdf.split`

Every tool is `read` or `act`. None is destructive, outward or shareable, so no app's agent can be granted one, not even under developer mode. Act tools write only inside their engine's area, and their descriptions say a file already at `out` is replaced.

### What is left out, and why

- **Declared, not granted:** `vector.run` and `effect.run` (`engines::HELD_FOR_REVIEW`). They are generic engine command doors that can run any command in the engine's catalog, so they get their own review. They are declared so the relay refuses them by name (`not_granted`). `vector.run`'s description mentions #405's plug-in refusal.
- **Not declared:** `design.commands`, `effect.commands`, `vector.commands`. They answer JSON arrays, and octos takes object results only. A future door review would need an object-wrapped catalog method.

## Hazards found and how each is handled

1. **Admission, a real blocker.** `admission::check("os.word")` fell through to the store path, because there is no system app or installed bundle with that id. The relay would have refused every engine call as `app_unavailable`. A virtual owner is now admitted as the shell's own compiled-in service. The check runs after the system-app check, so a future `os.<family>` system app would still be admitted as itself.
2. **Lazy bundle loads.** The relay never loads a bundle on a call. `ensure_loaded("card.os.<family>")` returns early because the catalog knows the owner. `script_apps::load` and `script_app_installed` fail in `admitted_bundle` before `install`, so they change nothing. An app that asks for an engine tool gets a grant on the virtual owner that can never be used. A test drives every one of those paths and proves each owner's declarations and executor are unchanged. Another test fails if `apps/<family>/bundle` or a packaging entry for an engine ever appears, so the virtual owner gets retired then rather than shadowed.
3. **Consent and approvals: no bypass was added.** First-use consent applies to an app's own agent (the relay checks it only for `CallerKind::AppPeer`). As with Calendar's tools, the system agent's calls are authorized by its reviewed grant. read and act tools raise no approval, and the tests assert `world.asked` stays empty. The tools are not `background`. octos runs them only in an attended turn, and the system session is attended.
4. **Settings and agents.** `apps::agent_apps` lists apps, not catalog owners. A test checks that no `os.<family>` shows up there, in `declared_octos`, or as a prepared peer.
5. **File flow: there is no sanctioned staging path, and a decision is needed.** `files.list`, `files.read` and `files.search` are read-only. They are offered only to an app's own peer, over that app's account folder, and never to the system agent. The system agent's octos workspace (`<home>/octos-home/.octos/workspace`) and the engine areas (`<home>/apps/.host/<family>`) are separate trees. I did not invent an import method. Every tool description says its paths are relative to that engine's own workspace, and files elsewhere on the device are not in it. In practice the agent can create with `word.new` and `deck.new`, convert, and inspect. The other engines have nothing to work on until a staging path exists. **A precondition for that path:** designcraft resolves data-merge sources by paths written inside the documents it opens. vectorcraft's SVG import reads the files that `<image>` links point to, relative to the SVG's folder. So outside documents must not reach those two engines until that is contained. With the current grant, nothing agent-written reaches either area.
6. **The kernel's 64-tool cap.** octos `MAX_APP_TOOLS` at the pinned rev is 64 host tools per registration, and a larger set is refused whole, which would leave the system agent with no host tools at all. The largest possible system set is now 63: 12 native system tools, `terminal.run`, 3 Calendar, 4 `agents.*`, and 43 engine tools. The new `session_set` puts the engine tools last and cuts them first past the cap, and logs what it dropped. One test keeps the whole grant within the cap. Another proves the cut order. **Only one tool of headroom is left**, which may deserve a decision: raise the cap in octos for host sessions, or narrow the grant.
7. **The test hook had the wrong owner.** `system_call_test` built calls without `app`, so `HostToolCall::parse` used the name's first segment (`calendar`, `word`) instead of the owner the kernel stamps (`os.calendar`, `os.word`). It now stamps the resolved owner.
8. **Long calls (not changed here; follow-up).** An engine call runs on the thread that dispatches it, which is the UI thread for a tool call, and it holds App Hub's service registry while it runs. That is also true for app calls today. A long `film.export` stalls the shell. The kernel waits 30 s for a host answer (an act call then ends `outcome_unknown`), and App Hub times the request out after 60 s while the export still finishes. The fix is a worker with per-method timeouts in the services. That is a behaviour change to every engine service (these ten, plus Sheets and Photo), so it is left out of this PR.

## Tests (all run on the PR head `67d5649b`)

- `cargo test --locked -p octosense-word-service -p octosense-deck-service -p octosense-cad-service -p octosense-light-service -p octosense-sound-service -p octosense-design-service -p octosense-film-service -p octosense-effect-service -p octosense-vector-service -p octosense-pdf-service`: **88 passed, 0 failed.** This includes the new manifest test in each crate. Design's and Film's tests also check the answers the shell cannot exercise itself, because no tool writes a layout document or a `.fcproj`.
- From `phone/`, `cargo test --locked --features mobile-apps -p octosense-shell host_tools`: **95 passed, 0 failed.** New tests:
  - `the_system_agent_reaches_the_engines_by_its_grant_and_never_their_doors`: a granted act call (`word.new`) and read call (`word.info`), `not_granted` for `vector.run`, `effect.run` and for an app's agent, and an error naming its file relative to the engine's area.
  - `every_engine_service_refuses_a_store_apps_identity`: each of the ten services answers "serves system apps only" to `org.example.<family>`.
  - `a_failed_bundle_load_never_clobbers_an_engines_virtual_owner`
  - `an_engines_virtual_owner_is_no_agent_app`
  - `every_granted_engine_tool_answers_within_its_declared_result`: all 39 granted tools that can get a fixture run on real files. The fixtures are the engines' own outputs where possible: Word's PDF, Vector's DXF, a 12x8 PNG, a PCM WAV, and an effect project made by its door as its own owner. Each call goes through the real relay, which checks every answer against its `output_schema`. Only the engines' areas get written.
  - In `engines.rs`: owner routing, the grant equals declared tools minus the held doors, the doors are declared, area-relative errors, and the no-shipped-app guard.
- From `phone/`, `… system_chat`: **74 passed** (new: `the_system_agents_whole_grant_fits_the_kernels_cap`, `over_the_kernels_cap_the_engines_tools_give_way_first`). `… apps::`: **39 passed**.
- `python3 tools/native_apps.py --check`: OK. `python3 tools/setup.py --check --cargo`: OK. `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'`: **142 tests OK**.
- `tools/ci-local.sh` was not run, by request (the merge train runs it).

## Live proof (one hidden instance, `67d5649b`)

`cargo build --locked -p octosense`, then `HOME=<scratch> MAKEPAD_HIDE_WINDOWS=1 MAKEPAD_REMOTE=127.0.0.1:8895 target/debug/octosense`. `/help` answered after about 1 s. No engine manifest was refused at startup. One `/event?data=system-call:<tool> <json>` went to each engine:

```
[system-call] word.info {"call_id":"system-call-1","error":{"kind":"app_error","message":"word.info: word: none.docx: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
[system-call] deck.info {"call_id":"system-call-2","error":{"kind":"app_error","message":"deck.info: none.pptx: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
[system-call] cad.info {"call_id":"system-call-3","error":{"kind":"app_error","message":"cad.info: none.dxf: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
[system-call] light.info {"call_id":"system-call-4","error":{"kind":"app_error","message":"light.info: `none.dng`: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
[system-call] sound.info {"call_id":"system-call-5","error":{"kind":"app_error","message":"sound.info: none.wav: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
[system-call] design.info {"call_id":"system-call-6","error":{"kind":"app_error","message":"design.info: none.designcraft: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
[system-call] film.info {"call_id":"system-call-7","error":{"kind":"app_error","message":"film.info: none.mp4: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
[system-call] effect.info {"call_id":"system-call-8","error":{"kind":"app_error","message":"effect.info: cannot read none.ecproj: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
[system-call] vector.info {"call_id":"system-call-9","error":{"kind":"app_error","message":"vector.info: none.svg: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
[system-call] pdf.info {"call_id":"system-call-10","error":{"kind":"app_error","message":"pdf.info: none.pdf: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
[system-call] light.controls {"call_id":"system-call-11","data":{"controls":[{"decimals":0,"default":100.0,"id":"profile.amount", … (114 controls, ok)
[system-call] vector.run: a test call runs only a declared read tool
```

Each engine answered with its own error for the missing file. None answered `not_granted`, `app_tool_unavailable`, `app_unavailable` or unknown tool. `light.controls` returned its real 114-control catalog, which passed its output schema. Before the error scrub, the same probe showed `effect.info: cannot read /…/wave2-probe-home/.octosense/apps/.host/effect/none.ecproj`. `curl /quit` answered `{"ok":1}`, and the process exited 0 about 2 s later.

## Docs

- Root `AGENTS.md`: the relay row now covers the virtual owners and `ENGINE_TOOLS`.
- `apps/AGENTS.md` ("Changing tools and data access"): which agents get which engine tools.
- `apps/README.md` and `apps/README.zh-CN.md`: an engine tools note under App agents, plus the layout line.
- ADR 0013, English and 简体中文: a dated "Agent tools (8 Oct 2026)" note covering the design, the grant, the exclusions, the file gap, the cap and long calls.
